title: Design and Visual Communications Foundations I
description: Architectural design principles; development of skills in perception, thought and craft as they apply to the formation of two- and three-dimensional relationships; introduction to and practice of tools, methods, techniques available for graphic communication; graphic communication and the design process; observation and other forms of free-hand drawing and drawing systems that develop representational and descriptive capabilities.
prerequisites: Prerequisites: BS in Architecture major.

title: Design and Visual Communication Foundations II
description: Approaches to problem identification and problem solving emphasizing human, physical and cultural factors influencing architectural design; understanding of space, materiality and tectonics in a human body scale; development of drawing methods with emphasis on analytical drawing; reinforcement of visual and verbal communication as applied to design processes.
prerequisites: Prerequisites: Grade of C or better in ARCH 105 ; major in BS in Architecture.

title: Visual Communication Foundations I
description: Introduction to and practice of tools, methods, techniques available for graphic communication; graphic communication and the design process; observation and other forms of free-hand drawing and drawing systems that develop representational and descriptive capabilities.

title: Architecture Design I
description: Issues and methods in designing environments for human habitation and well-being; projects addressing site, functional planning, spatial ordering, form generation through a recognition of the synthesis of space, structure, use and context; reinforcement of appropriate graphic and model building techniques.
prerequisites: Prerequisites: Grade of C or better in ARCH 105 and ARCH 106 .

title: Architecture Design II
description: Fundamental issues of innovative design processes and creation explored through the creative use of past, present and future materials, tools, and technologies; with an emphasis upon the research of materials, methods, scale, craft and technique as instruments of design, fabrication, and production.
prerequisites: Prerequisites: Grade of C or better in ARCH 205 .

title: Social and Behavioral Factors in Design
description: Social and behavioral factors in the built and natural environment; environmental perception and spatial cognition; social-environmental processes such as privacy and crowding; setting-oriented discussion on residences, education, and the workplace; the psychology of nature and natural resource management; social design and social science contribution to architectural design.

title: Sustainable Architecture
description: A comprehensive introduction to sustainability concepts, techniques and applications at all levels of the built environment, history of contemporary development of sustainable architecture from 1960 to the present; design strategies, environmental technologies and social factors for reducing building energy needs and carbon foot prints; global applications of sustainable approaches.

title: Computational Methods in Architecture
description: Software and processes for computation design in architecture; image editing and creation, vector drawing, 3D modeling, parametric modeling, rendering techniques and simulation.

title: Foundations of Museum Studies
description: COURSE OVERVIEW. An introduction to the interdisciplinary field of museum studies, exploring how museums collect, preserve, interpret and exhibit material culture to convey cultural, historical and scientific knowledge. Emphasizes museums as dynamic institutions shaped by ethical, educational and civic responsibilities and fosters critical inquiry into questions such as: Who do museums serve? How do objects acquire meaning? What responsibilities do museums have to communities and history? Provides a foundation for further study in museum work while developing skills in civic engagement, applied learning, collaboration, inclusion and leadership. Engages museums as spaces for dialogue and lifelong learning, encouraging reflection on how they shape public understanding and express broader social values. May incorporate topics that respond to current events, student interests or emerging issues in museum studies. TOPICS AND THEMES. May include: history and development of museums; collecting practices from antiquity to the present; analysis of museum organization, leadership structures and varying types of institutions; consideration of professional standards, collections stewardship; evaluation of interpretation, educational programming and strategies for access and inclusion; ethical, educational and civic responsibilities of museums.
prerequisites: Cross Listing: ANTH 221 and MUST 221 .

title: Foundations of Historic Preservation
description: Exploration and evaluation of the cross-disciplinary work of historic preservation; emphasis on the significance of historic places to societal well-being and conservation alternatives for historic and cultural environments; review of preservation projects and treatments; guest presentations and case studies from practicing professionals and researchers in a variety of fields.

title: Survey of World Architecture History I
description: (ARCH 1301) Survey of World Architecture History I. A survey of world architecture and the human-designed and built environment from prehistory to the 13th century.

title: Survey of World Architecture History II
description: (ARCH 1302) Survey of World Architecture History II. A survey of world architecture and the human-designed and built environment from the 13th to the 19th century.

title: Comparative Theory in the Built and Virtual Environments
description: Introduction of cultural theory and the environment; theories, special concepts and ideas relevant to the built and virtual environments with primary focus on the last fifty years; theory, theory building, and application to buildings and urban design; formation of ideas and critical ways of assessing the environment.

title: Seminar in Contemporary Architecture
description: Presentations by and discussions with professionals representing specialty areas related to environmental design through the Department of Architecture Lecture Series. May be taken four times for credit. Must be taken on a satisfactory/unsatisfactory basis.
repeatability: May be taken four times for credit.

title: Special Topics in...
description: Selected topics in an identified area of Architecture. May be repeated for credit.

title: Research in Architecture Innovation
description: Research conducted under the direction of faculty member in the College of Architecture. May be repeated 2 times for credit.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: Approval of instructor and department head.
repeatability: May be repeated 2 times for credit.

title: Architecture Design III
description: Integration of architectural theories and philosophy with environmental design systems; study of theoretical approaches to graphic and analytical thinking, problem identification and design dissemination through various media, case studies and problem resolution; conditions and forces associated with a variety of building types and the generation design solutions.
prerequisites: Prerequisites: Admission to upper level in BS in Architecture; ARCH 249 and ARCH 250 .

title: Digital Fabrication for Architecture
description: Digital fabrication for architecture including software, numerically controlled tools, translation applications and management strategies for digital fabrication workflows; production of building components from three dimensional datasets of virtual architecture proposals.
prerequisites: Prerequisites: Junior or senior classification or approval of instructor; ARCH 216 or approval of instructor.

title: Conceptual Structural Analysis
description: A non-mathematical investigation of structural systems and components with respect to behavior; selection of the most appropriate structural system for various building typologies.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: Junior or senior classification or approval of instructor.

title: Architectural Envelopes
description: Study of roof, wall, glazing and screen systems of significant works in contemporary architecture and the strategies behind their making; focus on innovative materials, surface effects, and performance aspects.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: Junior or senior classification in environmental design.

title: The Making of Architecture
description: Study of significant works of contemporary architecture and materials and strategies used in their making; focus on innovative materials, systems, and partnerships necessary to realize the design.
prerequisites: Prerequisites: Junior or senior classification in environmental design or approval of instructor or ARCH classification.

title: Architectural Structures
description: Physical principles that govern statics and strength of materials through the design of architectural structures from a holistic view, in the context of architectural ideas and examples; introduction to construction, behavior of materials, and design considerations for simple and complex structural assemblies; computer applications.
prerequisites: Prerequisites: Junior or senior classification in environmental design; MATH 142 or equivalent; PHYS 201 .

title: Architectural Systems
description: Theory and applications of building energy use, envelope design, shading analysis, heating and cooling systems, lighting design; building water supply, plumbing and drainage systems; electrical, acoustical, fire and lightning protection; life safety; transportation systems and construction materials; calculations, equipment selection, and component sizing as they relate to building design.
prerequisites: Prerequisites: Junior or senior classification in environmental design; PHYS 201 .

title: History of Building Technology
description: Chronological development of civilization and building technology from prehistoric cultures to present; classic and modern materials, structural devices past and present, machine-produced products, prefabrication, construction methodology and servicing.

title: Architecture, Heritage and Culture
description: Global exploration of how architecture and the built environment express culture and identity; theoretical and practical approaches to cultural heritage and conservation.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: Junior or senior classification.

title: Documentation of Historic Buildings and Sites
description: Techniques for recording historic buildings and sites; measuring and drawing to Historic American Building Survey Standards; field experience in photography, laser scanning, photogrammetry, hand measuring, field notes and record drawing preparation.
prerequisites: Prerequisites: Junior or senior classification or approval of instructor.

title: History and Theory of Modern and Contemporary Architecture
description: Development of modern and contemporary architecture in the 20th and 21st centuries; materials, structure, social and economic changes as well as architectural theory.
prerequisites: Prerequisites: Junior or senior classification.

title: History of Product Design
description: History of product design in Europe and America including the relationship between designer and object, the relationship of design, industry and media over time and design criticism; focus on material/technical and typological approaches, comparative method and content analysis in context of original environment and social history.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: Junior or senior classification or approval of instructor.

title: Topics in Design Build Community Service
description: Contemporary topics in architectural design-build practices including high impact interdisciplinary learning experiences developed through a project-based learning model with a focus on the planning, design, pre-construction, construction and project delivery; team-based approach with those outside of the architecture discipline to design, plan and complete project documents, estimates and undertake the construction activities necessary to make a fully functioning community service project.
prerequisites: Prerequisites: Junior or senior classification or approval of instructor.

title: Design Seminar
description: Presentations by and discussions with professionals representing specialty areas related to architectural fabrication and product design. May be taken three times for credit.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: Junior or senior classification or approval of instructor.
repeatability: May be taken three times for credit.

title: Design Creativity
description: Fundamental critical and creative thinking skills needed to participate in and create the future; study of how design can impact the physical environment and society.
prerequisites: Prerequisites: Junior or senior classification or approval of instructor.

title: Architecture Design IV
description: A comprehensive design studio focused on the integration of design theory with functionally sustainable environmental and structural systems; consideration of a project from site analysis and programming through design detailing.
prerequisites: Prerequisites: ARCH 305 , ARCH 331 , ARCH 335 ; CARC 301 or ARCH 494 ; concurrent enrollment in ARCH 431 and ARCH 435 .

title: Architecture Design V
description: Topical approaches to design, emphasizing theory and practice of architecture or related disciplines, such as urban design, interior design, health care design, etc.
prerequisites: Prerequisites: Junior or senior classification; admission to upper level in BS in Architecture; grade of C or better in ARCH 305 , ARCH 331 and ARCH 335 ; grade of C or better in CARC 301 or ARCH 494 ; students may with approval of the department enroll in the course during the summer term prior to taking ARCH 405 , ARCH 431 and ARCH 435 if they are within 20 credit hours of graduation prior to the beginning of the following fall semester.

title: Elements of Urban Design
description: Investigation of design elements shaping the urban environment; emphasis placed on contemporary precedents in architecture, landscape and urbanism to evaluate design complexity on multiple levels: social, political, environmental, economic, cultural and geographic.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: Admission to upper level division in BED or BS-URPN.

title: Energy and Sustainable Architecture
description: Understanding the various design decisions impacting sustainability and energy efficiency; includes participation in an "academic" LEED-NC rating project; interdisciplinary team approach with a design studio architect to perform the LEED-NC rating on the architect's building; application of reference material, standards, and USGBC material.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: Junior and senior classification or approval of instructor.

title: History of Ancient Architecture in the Near East, Egypt, Greece and Rome
description: Examination of stylistic, structural and theoretical advancements in ancient architecture, with case studies from the Near East, Egypt, Greece and Rome.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: ARCH 249 or ARTS 149 ; junior or senior classification or approval of degree coordinator or instructor.

title: Integrated Structures
description: Selection and economics of structural systems in the context of integrating structural systems into a building through good design; analysis and design of wood, steel, concrete, and composite systems and members in relation to building design.
prerequisites: Prerequisites: Admission to upper level in environmental design; ARCH 305 , ARCH 331 , ARCH 335 ; concurrent enrollment in ARCH 405 and ARCH 435 .

title: Architectural Lighting
description: Theory and practice of lighting design as an art and science; aperture design for sunlight control; selecting and locating luminaries to enhance interior and exterior surfaces and spaces.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: ARCH 335 or junior or senior classification in EDAS.

title: The Role of Sculpture and Painting in Ancient Architecture
description: Interrelationships of architecture, painting and sculpture in the ancient world including Egypt, Mesopotamia, Crete, Greece and Rome.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: ARCH 249 or ARTS 149 ; junior or senior classification or approval of degree coordinator or instructor.

title: Integrated Systems
description: Understanding how to integrate sustainable environmental systems into a building through good design; lectures support studio; systems faculty participate in studio critiques throughout the project.
prerequisites: Prerequisites: Admission to upper level in environmental design; ARCH 305 , ARCH 331 , ARCH 335 ; concurrent enrollment in ARCH 405 and ARCH 431 .

title: The Gothic Cathedral
description: A critical study of monumental church-building in Europe during the later Middle Ages (ca. 1140–1500 C.E.); investigation of works of architecture, sculpture and painting in relation to issues of craft, ritual and power; exploration of the afterlives of the Gothic style in the Americas, Asia and Africa.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: ARCH 250 or ARTS 150 ; junior or senior classification or approval of degree coordinator or instructor.

title: World Religious Architecture
description: Exploration of the diverse architectural traditions of the world’s major religions with an emphasis on issues of place-making, representation, ritual, identity, and culture, past and present.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: Junior or senior classification.

title: Baroque and Rococo Architecture
description: The investigation of the history of architecture, the arts and society, and major creative individuals from the late sixteenth to the early eighteenth centuries.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: ARCH 250 or ARTS 150 ; junior or senior classification or approval of degree coordinator or instructor.

title: Aegean Art and Architecture
description: Art and architecture of the prehistoric Aegean, ca. 6000-1100-B.C.E.; focus on the built environment, material culture and visual arts of early civilization in the Aegean basin; evidence for regional and vernacular architectural traditions; expressions of power, ideology and social identity through monumental architectural and elite arts of Minoan Crete and Mycenaean Greece.
prerequisites: Prerequisites: Junior or senior classification; approval of instructor or degree coordinator.

title: American Architecture
description: Investigation of indigenous, vernacular and historical American architecture from 1500 to 1920; evolution of construction technologies, changing building forms and finish treatments; identification of historic architectural styles and their influence on 21st century American architecture.
prerequisites: Prerequisites: ARCH 250 or ARCH 350 ; junior or senior classification, or approval of instructor.

title: Strategies in Architectural Management
description: Emerging strategies in the architecture and construction industry, with an emphasis on understanding the changing structure of the industry and the management of both firms and projects.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: Senior classification or approval of degree coordinator.

title: Careers in Architecture
description: Career opportunities in the profession of architecture; investigations into the composition of architectural practice today and the wide range of specialties represented in architectural firms; interviews with select representative individuals.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: Admission to upper level in environmental design, construction science or landscape architecture.

title: Ethics and Professional Practice
description: Issues and relationships within the business, legal and political environment; introduction to the concepts of architectural specifications and the AIA standard conditions of the construction contract; forms of construction, bidding and contract documents. For undergraduate students pursuing a professional degree and a career in architecture.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: Senior classification in environmental design.

title: Cultural and Ethical Considerations for Global Practice
description: Issues and relationships within the cultural, business, legal and political environments of global practice; differences in the construction contract, bidding and various forms of construction.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: Junior or senior classification.

title: Elements of Interior Architecture
description: Analysis and design of architectural interiors; historical and professional perspectives incorporating programming, space planning and organization; specification and selection of furnishings and materials to satisfy user needs in residential, commercial and institutional settings.
prerequisites: Prerequisites: Admission to upper level in environmental design; concurrent enrollment in ARCH 405 , ARCH 431 and ARCH 435 not allowed.

title: Preservation Field Studies
description: Fieldwork related to practice of historic preservation and cultural heritage management; methods of documentation, analysis, planning and treatment; emphasis on identification and evaluation of multidisciplinary approaches to historic preservation and heritage conservation in global contexts; topics vary each semester. May be taken for credit up to six hours.
prerequisites: Prerequisites: ARCH 246 , ARCH 346 , or ARCH 347 ; junior or senior classification or approval of instructor.
repeatability: May be taken for credit up to six hours.

title: Seminar
description: Presentations by and discussions with professionals representing specialty areas related to environmental design; career and academic objectives. May be repeated for up to 4 credit hours. Must be taken on a satisfactory/unsatisfactory basis.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: Junior or senior classification or approval of instructor.
repeatability: May be repeated for up to 4 credit hours.

title: Summer Internship
description: Practical experience in an office of design allied professionals; 10- week internship with a minimum of 400 hours continuous employment; departmental pre-approval through the departmental internship coordinator required; post evaluation conducted following the internship. May not be repeated for credit.
prerequisites: Prerequisites: Junior or senior classification or approval of instructor; approval of the environmental design internship coordinator.
repeatability: May not be repeated for credit.

title: Directed Studies
description: Special projects in architecture. May be repeated for credit.
prerequisites: Prerequisites: Admission to upper level in environmental design; approval of instructor and degree coordinator.

title: Special Topics in...
description: Special topics in an identified area of architecture. May be repeated for credit.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: Junior or senior classification; approval of instructor and degree coordinator.

title: Advanced Architecture Innovation Research
description: Research conducted under the direction of faculty member in the College of Architecture. May be repeated 2 times for credit.
prerequisites: Prerequisite: Admission to upper level in environmental design; approval of instructor and department head.
repeatability: May be repeated 2 times for credit.

title: Internship
description: Practical experience in an office of design allied professionals; fifteen week internship with a minimum of 600 hours of continuous employment; departmental pre-approval through the departmental internship coordinator required; post evaluation conducted following the internship. To be taken only as a requirement for the study away semester. May not be repeated for credit.
prerequisites: Prerequisites: Junior or senior classification; admission to upper level in environmental design; CARC 481 ; approval of the environmental design internship coordinator.
repeatability: May not be repeated for credit.
